sounds.name: Chordal
sounds.ref: Suren Forward’s “Chordal” patch sheet for the Malevolent
sounds.blurb: A bright, shifting two-oscillator tone whose colour changes up the keyboard, with harder notes brighter.
sounds.how: VCO 2’s pulse width follows the keys, so each note has a different hollowness, while the LFO sweeps VCO 1’s. VCO 1’s saw also goes round the mixer a second time through AUX, and velocity, not the envelope, opens the filter. The patch sheet records only the cables and the wave buttons, so the knob settings here are this lesson’s, chosen to make the patch speak.

steps.title: Two VCOs, three waves
steps.why:
VCO 1 sounds its saw and pulse together, VCO 2 its saw, a fifth above.
- VCO 1 SAW and PULSE buttons lit: the two waves mix at its OUT.
- VCO 1 LEVEL 8, VCO 2 LEVEL 7: both into the mixer.
- VCO 2 SAW lit, COARSE 5.7 (a fifth up): the interval gives the patch its chordal sound.
- Listen for: a bright, buzzy fifth.

steps.title: Pulse widths that move
steps.why:
Two cables set the pulse widths moving: the LFO on VCO 1’s, the keys on VCO 2’s.
- LFO TRIANGLE into VCO 1 SHAPE, with SHAPE MOD at 4: the same as the normal, made visible.
- KEYS PITCH into VCO 2 SHAPE, with SHAPE MOD at 6: higher notes give a thinner pulse.
- LFO RATE 3: a slow sweep.
- Listen for: a gentle movement in VCO 1, and a different colour on each key.

steps.title: The saw again, through AUX
steps.why:
VCO 1’s saw is patched into the mixer’s AUX as well, so it is heard twice, louder than its pulse.
- VCO 1 SAW into AUX, AUX LEVEL 5.
- Listen for: more edge in the mix.

steps.title: Velocity on the filter
steps.why:
With KEYS VELOCITY in the VCF’s FM 1, Envelope 1 no longer reaches the filter: how hard each key is played sets its brightness.
- KEYS VELOCITY into VCF FM 1, FM 1 at 5.
- CUT OFF 4, RESONANCE 3: a darker base for velocity to open.
- Listen for: soft notes dull, hard ones bright.

steps.title: A keyboard envelope
steps.why:
Envelope 2 shapes the loudness through AM 1.
- ATTACK 0, SUSTAIN 10, RELEASE 4: notes start at once, hold, and ring on a little.
- Listen for: chords that overlap gently.

context.vco2.shapeMod: In this sound: how much the key pitch changes VCO 2’s width.
context.vcf.fm1: In this sound: how far velocity opens the filter.
context.mix.aux: In this sound: the second copy of VCO 1’s saw.

tweaks.hear: The colour changes much more from key to key, thin at the top.
Every note is equally dark, however hard it is played.

sounds.name: Extreme
sounds.ref: Suren Forward’s “Extreme” patch sheet for the Malevolent
sounds.blurb: A pulse that shapes itself and leaps between two pitches, getting louder up the keyboard.
sounds.how: VCO 1’s triangle moves its own pulse width at audio rate, which roughens it, and the LFO square replaces the keys at its 1V/OCT, so it jumps between two pitches whatever is played. VCO 2’s triangle still follows the keys, and KEYS PITCH replaces Envelope 2 at the VCA, so higher notes are louder and notes below middle C are silent. The patch sheet records only the cables and the wave buttons, so the knob settings here are this lesson’s, chosen to make the patch speak.

steps.title: A pulse and a triangle
steps.why:
VCO 1 on its pulse alone, VCO 2 on its triangle.
- VCO 1 SAW off, PULSE lit, LEVEL 7.
- VCO 2 TRIANGLE lit, LEVEL 6.
- Listen for: a hollow pulse over a soft triangle.

steps.title: VCO 1 shapes itself
steps.why:
VCO 1’s own triangle into its SHAPE input moves its pulse width at the pitch it plays.
- VCO 1 TRIANGLE into VCO 1 SHAPE, SHAPE MOD 6.
- Listen for: a rougher, more nasal pulse.

steps.title: The LFO plays VCO 1
steps.why:
The LFO square into VCO 1’s 1V/OCT takes the keys away from it: it now jumps between two pitches at LFO RATE, whatever is played.
- LFO SQUARE into VCO 1 1V/OCT.
- LFO RATE 4: a few jumps a second.
- Listen for: VCO 1 trilling on its own while VCO 2 plays the tune.

steps.title: Louder up the keyboard
steps.why:
KEYS PITCH into AM 1 replaces Envelope 2: the VCA opens as far as the key is high.
- KEYS PITCH into AM 1, AM 1 at 4.
- CUT OFF 10, RESONANCE 0: the filter stays open.
- Envelope 2 ATTACK 0, SUSTAIN 10, RELEASE 2: set, though the VCA no longer follows it.
- Listen for: high notes loud, notes below middle C silent, and the sound carrying on after the keys are let go, because the pitch voltage stays at the last key.

context.lfo.rate: In this sound: how fast VCO 1 jumps.
context.vca.am1: In this sound: how loud the key pitch makes the VCA.

tweaks.hear: The jumps become a buzz, and VCO 1 turns into a rough second tone.

sounds.name: FM Phasers
sounds.ref: Suren Forward’s “FM Phasers” patch sheet for the Malevolent
sounds.blurb: Every wave of both VCOs at once, VCO 1 shaped by its own saw, with a tremolo that speeds up the keyboard.
sounds.how: All six wave buttons are lit, so both VCOs send their saw, triangle and pulse. VCO 1’s saw moves its own pulse width, KEYS PITCH replaces the LFO at AM 2, and velocity replaces Envelope 1 at the filter. The patch sheet records only the cables and the wave buttons, so the knob settings here are this lesson’s, chosen to make the patch speak.

steps.title: Every wave
steps.why:
All three buttons on both VCOs: each sends its saw, triangle and pulse together.
- VCO 1 SAW, TRIANGLE and PULSE lit, LEVEL 6.
- VCO 2 SAW, TRIANGLE and PULSE lit, LEVEL 6, FINE 5.3: a little sharp, so the two phase.
- Listen for: a thick, phasing tone.

steps.title: VCO 1 shapes itself
steps.why:
VCO 1’s saw into its own SHAPE moves its pulse width at audio rate.
- VCO 1 SAW into VCO 1 SHAPE, SHAPE MOD 5.
- Listen for: a harder, FM-like edge.

steps.title: Velocity on the filter
steps.why:
KEYS VELOCITY replaces Envelope 1 at the VCF’s FM 1.
- KEYS VELOCITY into VCF FM 1, FM 1 at 4.
- CUT OFF 5, RESONANCE 4.
- Listen for: harder notes brighter and more vocal.

steps.title: Pitch into AM 2
steps.why:
KEYS PITCH replaces the LFO at AM 2, so the VCA opens further on high notes; Envelope 2 still shapes each note through AM 1, patched here as the sheet draws it.
- ENV 2 OUT into AM 1: the same as the normal.
- KEYS PITCH into AM 2, AM 2 at 3.
- Envelope 2 ATTACK 0, SUSTAIN 10, RELEASE 2.
- Listen for: the higher notes standing out, and a quiet tone left sounding after the keys come up: the pitch voltage stays at the last key, so AM 2 keeps the VCA a little open.

context.vco1.shapeMod: In this sound: how far VCO 1’s saw moves its own pulse width.

tweaks.hear: VCO 1 turns harsh and clangy.

sounds.name: Plink
sounds.ref: Suren Forward’s “Plink” patch sheet for the Malevolent
sounds.blurb: A short, glassy pluck: the mix through the low-pass and the band-pass at once, with VCO 2 rippling the cutoff.
sounds.how: MIX OUT goes into the BAND PASS input as well as, through the normal, the LOW PASS one, so the mix is filtered both ways at once into the one output. VCO 2’s saw ripples the cutoff at audio rate, velocity sets VCO 2’s pulse width, and a short envelope makes it a pluck. The patch sheet records only the cables and the wave buttons, so the knob settings here are this lesson’s, chosen to make the patch speak.

steps.title: Two saws
steps.why:
VCO 1 and VCO 2 on their saws, VCO 2 an octave up.
- VCO 1 SAW lit, LEVEL 7.
- VCO 2 SAW lit, LEVEL 5, COARSE 6.25 (an octave up).
- Listen for: a bright, buzzy octave.

steps.title: Two shapes
steps.why:
The LFO moves VCO 1’s pulse width (as the normal does) and velocity sets VCO 2’s. Neither VCO plays its pulse here, so this is the sheet’s wiring more than something to hear.
- LFO TRIANGLE into VCO 1 SHAPE, KEYS VELOCITY into VCO 2 SHAPE.
- Listen for: no change yet.

steps.title: Low-pass and band-pass at once
steps.why:
MIX OUT into BAND PASS: the mix now reaches the filter twice, low-passed through the normal and band-passed through the cable, added at the one output.
- MIX OUT into BAND PASS.
- CUT OFF 5, RESONANCE 6: a ringing band in the middle.
- Listen for: a vocal, nasal ring on top of the low-pass body.

steps.title: VCO 2 ripples the cutoff
steps.why:
VCO 2’s saw into the VCF’s FM 1 replaces Envelope 1: the cutoff moves at VCO 2’s pitch.
- VCO 2 SAW into VCF FM 1, FM 1 at 2.
- Listen for: a glassy, metallic edge.

steps.title: A pluck
steps.why:
Envelope 2 falls away quickly with no sustain.
- ATTACK 0, DECAY 3, SUSTAIN 0, RELEASE 3.
- Listen for: short plinks that ring off.

context.vcf.res: In this sound: how glassy the band-pass rings.
context.vcf.fm1: In this sound: how much VCO 2 ripples the cutoff.

tweaks.hear: The ripple turns into a clangy, bell-like FM tone.

sounds.name: Sentient Bass
sounds.ref: Suren Forward’s “Sentient Bass” patch sheet for the Malevolent
sounds.blurb: A thick, restless bass: the mix through the low-pass and the high-pass together, opened by velocity.
sounds.how: Both VCOs send their saw and triangle, low, with VCO 1’s pulse width on the LFO. MIX OUT goes into the HIGH PASS input too, so the filter gives its low-pass and its high-pass of the same mix at once, and velocity replaces the LFO at the VCF’s FM 2. The patch sheet records only the cables and the wave buttons, so the knob settings here are this lesson’s, chosen to make the patch speak.

steps.title: Saws and triangles, low
steps.why:
Both VCOs on their saw and triangle, two octaves down.
- VCO 1 SAW and TRIANGLE lit, LEVEL 7, COARSE 2.5.
- VCO 2 SAW and TRIANGLE lit, LEVEL 7, COARSE 2.5, FINE 5.2.
- Listen for: a big, slightly beating bass.

steps.title: Low-pass and high-pass at once
steps.why:
MIX OUT into HIGH PASS: the filter now gives the mix low-passed and high-passed together.
- MIX OUT into HIGH PASS.
- LFO TRIANGLE into VCO 1 SHAPE, as the sheet draws it.
- CUT OFF 3, RESONANCE 5: round lows, with a rasp of highs on top.
- Listen for: a hollow, hard-edged bass.

steps.title: Velocity on the cutoff
steps.why:
KEYS VELOCITY into the VCF’s FM 2 replaces the LFO: harder notes move the cutoff up, which darkens the high-pass and opens the low-pass.
- KEYS VELOCITY into VCF FM 2, FM 2 at 4.
- Listen for: each note’s character following how hard it is played.

steps.title: A bass envelope
steps.why:
- Envelope 2 ATTACK 0, DECAY 4, SUSTAIN 6, RELEASE 2.
- Listen for: a firm start that settles.

context.vcf.cutoff: In this sound: where the low-pass ends and the high-pass begins.

tweaks.hear: The balance moves from a rasp of highs to a full, round low end.

sounds.name: Tangerine
sounds.ref: Suren Forward’s “Tangerine” patch sheet for the Malevolent
sounds.blurb: A bright lead whose filter follows the keys, opened by firm notes and closed by soft ones.
sounds.how: KEYS PITCH replaces Envelope 1 at the VCF’s FM 1, so the cutoff follows the keys, and KEYS VELOCITY replaces the key gate at Envelope 2. The velocity voltage holds after the key is let go, so a note played harder than half way opens the VCA and keeps it open, and one played softer closes it. VCO 1’s saw and triangle sound with VCO 2’s saw. The patch sheet records only the cables and the wave buttons, so the knob settings here are this lesson’s, chosen to make the patch speak.

steps.title: Three waves
steps.why:
VCO 1 sends its saw and triangle, VCO 2 its saw, a touch sharp.
- VCO 1 SAW and TRIANGLE lit, LEVEL 7.
- VCO 2 SAW lit, LEVEL 6, FINE 5.4.
- Listen for: a full, gently beating tone.

steps.title: The filter follows the keys
steps.why:
KEYS PITCH into the VCF’s FM 1 replaces Envelope 1, so higher notes open the filter further.
- KEYS PITCH into VCF FM 1, FM 1 at 1.25: about an octave of cutoff per octave played.
- CUT OFF 5, RESONANCE 4.
- LFO TRIANGLE into VCO 1 SHAPE, as the sheet draws it.
- Listen for: the tone staying as bright across the keyboard.

steps.title: Velocity gates the loudness
steps.why:
KEYS VELOCITY into Envelope 2’s GATE replaces the key gate: the envelope is held while the velocity voltage is past half way, and that voltage stays where the last key left it.
- KEYS VELOCITY into ENV 2 GATE.
- Envelope 2 ATTACK 0, SUSTAIN 9, RELEASE 3.
- Listen for: firm notes running into one another, and the soft last note letting the sound go.

steps.title: Velocity gates the loudness

- KEYS VELOCITY into ENV 2 GATE.

- Listen for: firm notes running into one another, and the soft last note letting the sound go.

sounds.name: Twin
sounds.ref: Suren Forward’s “Twin” patch sheet for the Malevolent
sounds.blurb: Every wave of VCO 1 over VCO 2’s triangle, with Envelope 2 sweeping VCO 1’s pitch and a thump of velocity through the high-pass.
sounds.how: Envelope 2 replaces the LFO at VCO 1’s FM 2, so every note starts with a pitch swoop, and KEYS VELOCITY goes into the HIGH PASS input as a sound of its own: a step that thumps at the start of each note. The sheet also draws an outside clock into Envelope 1’s GATE; that is left out here. The patch sheet records only the cables and the wave buttons, so the knob settings here are this lesson’s, chosen to make the patch speak.

steps.title: Every wave of VCO 1
steps.why:
- VCO 1 SAW, TRIANGLE and PULSE lit, LEVEL 7.
- VCO 2 TRIANGLE lit, LEVEL 6, COARSE 3.75 (an octave down).
- LFO TRIANGLE into VCO 1 SHAPE, SHAPE MOD 3.
- Listen for: a rich lead over a soft octave below.

steps.title: Envelope 2 swoops VCO 1
steps.why:
ENV 2 OUT into VCO 1’s FM 2 replaces the LFO there.
- ENV 2 OUT into VCO 1 FM 2, FM 2 at 2.
- Envelope 2 ATTACK 0, DECAY 3, SUSTAIN 10, RELEASE 2: it rises at once, so VCO 1 starts sharp and stays there while the key is held.
- Listen for: VCO 1 jumping up against VCO 2 on every note.

steps.title: A thump through the high-pass
steps.why:
KEYS VELOCITY into HIGH PASS: a velocity step at the start of each note, high-passed, is a click.
- KEYS VELOCITY into HIGH PASS.
- CUT OFF 6, RESONANCE 5: the click rings a little at the cutoff.
- Listen for: a knock at the front of every note.

context.vco1.fm2: In this sound: how far Envelope 2 lifts VCO 1.

sounds.name: Nasty Bass FX
sounds.ref: Paul Whittington’s “Nasty Bass FX” patch sheet for the Malevolent
sounds.blurb: A snarling, self-oscillating bass: VCO 1 heard only as FM on VCO 2, through the low-pass and high-pass together.
sounds.how: VCO 1 has no wave lit, so it is silent in the mixer, and its triangle is used only to frequency-modulate VCO 2 through FM 2. MIX OUT also goes into the HIGH PASS input, and the resonance is high enough that the filter rings on its own. The knob settings follow the sheet’s drawn pointers, which are approximate; the tuning is set by ear, because this app’s COARSE range is its own.

steps.title: VCO 2 alone in the mixer
steps.why:
VCO 1’s saw goes off and VCO 2’s comes on, low: VCO 1 will be used only as a modulator.
- VCO 1 SAW off, LEVEL 1.
- VCO 2 SAW lit, LEVEL 8.3, COARSE 2.5, FINE 5.
- Listen for: one low saw.

steps.title: VCO 1 modulates VCO 2
steps.why:
VCO 1’s triangle into VCO 2’s FM 2 replaces the LFO there, at audio rate; Envelope 1 still reaches VCO 2 through FM 1.
- VCO 1 TRIANGLE into VCO 2 FM 2, FM 2 at 5.4.
- VCO 1 COARSE 2.6: just off VCO 2, so the FM beats and growls.
- VCO 2 FM 1 at 5.5, with Envelope 1 ATTACK 1, DECAY 5, SUSTAIN 0.5, RELEASE 1: a pitch drop on every note.
- Listen for: a clangy, growling bass.

steps.title: A ringing filter, two ways
steps.why:
MIX OUT into HIGH PASS adds the high-pass of the mix to the low-pass, and the resonance is high enough for the filter to ring on its own.
- MIX OUT into HIGH PASS.
- CUT OFF 3.3, RESONANCE 9, the VCF’s FM 1 at 3.3: Envelope 1 sweeps it on each note.
- Listen for: a whistling, snarling edge on the bass.

steps.title: A long release
steps.why:
- Envelope 2 ATTACK 1, DECAY 1, SUSTAIN 9.5, RELEASE 8.3.
- MASTER VOL 5: the ringing filter is loud, and the sheet sets the volume low too.
- Listen for: the notes hanging on after each key.

context.vco2.fm2: In this sound: how much VCO 1 growls into VCO 2.
context.vcf.res: In this sound: high enough for the filter to whistle.

tweaks.hear: The whistle goes, leaving the growl.

sounds.name: Reece Bass
sounds.ref: Paul Whittington’s “Reece Bass” patch sheet for the Malevolent
sounds.blurb: A wide, detuned bass: VCO 2’s pulse cross-modulating VCO 1’s saw, opened by velocity.
sounds.how: VCO 1’s saw and VCO 2’s pulse play nearly in tune, so they beat, and VCO 2’s OUT replaces Envelope 1 at VCO 1’s FM 1, cross-modulating it. Velocity replaces the LFO at the VCF’s FM 2. The knob settings follow the sheet’s drawn pointers, which are approximate; the tuning is set by ear, because this app’s COARSE range is its own.

steps.title: A saw and a pulse, nearly in tune
steps.why:
- VCO 1 SAW lit, LEVEL 9.4, COARSE 2.5, FINE 4.8.
- VCO 2 PULSE lit, LEVEL 9.3, COARSE 2.5, FINE 5.5: a little sharp of VCO 1.
- Listen for: two low tones beating against each other.

steps.title: Cross-modulation
steps.why:
VCO 2’s OUT into VCO 1’s FM 1 replaces Envelope 1 there.
- VCO 2 OUT into VCO 1 FM 1, FM 1 at 2.
- Listen for: a grittier, moving texture.

steps.title: Velocity opens it
steps.why:
KEYS VELOCITY into the VCF’s FM 2 replaces the LFO.
- KEYS VELOCITY into VCF FM 2, FM 2 at 6.7.
- CUT OFF 1.7, RESONANCE 7: dark, with a ringing peak.
- Listen for: soft notes a dull rumble, hard notes snarling.

steps.title: Envelope 2
steps.why:
- ATTACK 1, DECAY 1, SUSTAIN 9.5, RELEASE 1.7.
- DRIVE 1: a little warmth.
- Listen for: a solid, sustained bass.

context.vco2.fine: In this sound: the detune that makes the Reece beat.

sounds.name: Sweet Lead
sounds.ref: Paul Whittington’s “Sweet Lead” patch sheet for the Malevolent
sounds.blurb: Two triangles and VCO 1’s pulse through AUX, into a resonant filter that velocity opens.
sounds.how: Both VCOs play their triangles, and VCO 1’s pulse is added through the AUX input as a third voice. The resonance is high, and velocity replaces the LFO at the VCF’s FM 2, so harder notes sing. The knob settings follow the sheet’s drawn pointers, which are approximate; the tuning is set by ear, because this app’s COARSE range is its own.

steps.title: Two triangles
steps.why:
- VCO 1 SAW off and TRIANGLE lit, LEVEL 6.9, FINE 4.6.
- VCO 2 TRIANGLE lit, LEVEL 8.3, COARSE 6.25 (an octave up), FINE 5.2.
- Listen for: a soft, flute-like pair.

steps.title: VCO 1’s pulse through AUX
steps.why:
VCO 1’s pulse jack works whatever its buttons say: patched into AUX it is a third voice.
- VCO 1 PULSE into AUX, AUX LEVEL 5.
- Listen for: more body and edge.

steps.title: A singing filter
steps.why:
KEYS VELOCITY into the VCF’s FM 2 replaces the LFO.
- KEYS VELOCITY into VCF FM 2, FM 2 at 7.2.
- CUT OFF 3.5, RESONANCE 7.5.
- Listen for: harder notes brighter and ringing.

steps.title: A lead envelope
steps.why:
- Envelope 2 ATTACK 0.6, DECAY 1, SUSTAIN 9.5, RELEASE 1.5.
- Listen for: a soft start and a quick stop.

context.vcf.fm2: In this sound: how far velocity opens the filter.

sounds.name: Two Filters
sounds.ref: In the style of ambient music
sounds.blurb: VCO 1 low-passed and VCO 2 high-passed at the same time, through the one filter.

steps.why:

steps.title: VCO 2 into the high-pass
steps.why:

steps.title: The LFO moves the cutoff

steps.title: A slow pad envelope

steps.why:
- VCO 1 SAW and PULSE lit, LEVEL 6, COARSE 3.75 (an octave down).
- VCO 2 SAW lit, LEVEL 6, COARSE 3.75, FINE 5.1: slowly beating against VCO 1.
- Listen for: a low, rolling drone.

steps.title: The LFO on the shape and filter
steps.why:
- VCO 1 SHAPE MOD 5, VCF FM 2 at 1.5, LFO RATE 1.5: a slow sweep.
- CUT OFF 4, RESONANCE 4.
- Listen for: the drone slowly opening and closing.

steps.title: Drone
steps.why:

sounds.name: Gliding Solo
sounds.ref: In the style of Emerson, Lake & Palmer — “Lucky Man”
sounds.blurb: A fat, soaring solo lead that swoops slowly between every note.
sounds.how: On the Malevolent, pushing the joystick up is glide: the further up, the slower. Held at 0.65 every note slides from the last. A vibrato from the LFO triangle through both VCOs’ FM 2 makes the long notes sing.

steps.title: Saw and pulse

- VCO 2 PULSE lit, LEVEL 7, FINE 5.2.
- CUT OFF 6, RESONANCE 2.

steps.title: Vibrato
steps.why:
The LFO triangle reaches both VCOs’ FM 2 inside.
- VCO 1 FM 2 0.8, VCO 2 FM 2 0.8: about a third of a semitone.
- LFO RATE 6: about five times a second.
- Envelope 2 RELEASE 3.
- Listen for: long notes singing. Envelope 2’s SUSTAIN stays at 10.

sounds.name: Breathy Flute
sounds.ref: In the style of Jethro Tull — Ian Anderson
sounds.blurb: A breathy, overblown rock flute: the tone through the low-pass, the breath through the band-pass.
sounds.how: The filter has three inputs, each filtered its own way into one output. The triangle goes through the low-pass as usual, while the noise is patched straight into the BAND PASS input, so only a band of breath round the cutoff gets through. The LFO adds a flutter of vibrato.

- NOISE into BAND PASS.
- RESONANCE 2.
- Listen for: a band of breath riding on the tone.

- Envelope 2 ATTACK 3, RELEASE 2.

- Listen for: a thin, buzzing reed.

A cable replaces Envelope 1 at the VCF’s FM 1.
- KEYS PITCH into VCF FM 1, VCF FM 1 at 1.25: the band moves an octave for each octave played.
- CUT OFF 6.3, RESONANCE 4.
- MASTER VOL 9.
- Listen for: a plaintive, nasal tone, the same on every note.
